# Singapore Company Formation

## ![Image 5: Bermuda Exempt Company](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/home-icon.png)Singapore Limited Liability Company (Pte Ltd) Company Incorporation

Singapore is one of the fastest growing and most stable economies in the world, offering an incredibly safe and competitive environment for new incorporations. The World Bank ranked Singapore the best country in which to do business for two years running and ranked it the second most competitive after the USA. Benefits for incorporating a new company in Singapore include a tax exemption on the first SGD 100,000 profit.

## ![Image 7: Bermuda company formation name](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/company_name.png)Company Name

All company names must be approved by the Registry of Companies & Businesses. If approved, they may be reserved for two months. Company names must end with the suffix Pte Ltd or Ltd. We are able to conduct a company name check to ensure your proposed name is not identical to another company already incorporated.

All companies must have a registered office in Singapore where all correspondence may be sent. This is also where company accounts and registers shall be kept. The registered office must be open and accessible to the public for a minimum of three hours, between 0900 and 1700 on weekdays.

## ![Image 9: Bermuda Incorporation director](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Directors.png)Directors

Only one director is required to incorporate in Singapore, although as most banks and financial institutions in Singapore require two signatories it is recommended to have at least two directors. At least one director must be resident in Singapore but may be of any nationality and there are no restrictions on the nationality or residency of other directors. Companies are required to maintain a directors’ register which is available for public inspection.

## ![Image 11: Bermuda company formation shareholder](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Shareholders.png)Shareholders

Only a single shareholder is required and there are no restrictions on nationality or residency; a shareholder may also hold a directorship position in the company. A maximum of fifty shareholders is allowed and corporate entities are permitted. Should a shareholder be a national of China, Pakistan, Bangladesh or certain other countries, the registry may ask for further information. A shareholder register is kept and available for public inspection.

## ![Image 13: company formation secretary](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Company-Secretary.png)Company Secretary

As per section 171 of the Singapore Companies Act, every company must appoint a qualified company secretary within 6 months of its incorporation and the secretary must be resident in Singapore. In the case of a sole director/shareholder, the same person cannot act as the company secretary.

## ![Image 15: Bermuda company formation share capital](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)Share Capital

The minimum share capital is SGD 1, there is no maximum share capital.

## ![Image 17: Bermuda company incorporation timescale](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)Timescale

The process to incorporate usually takes around three days, but if shareholders are nationals of China, Pakistan and other certain countries it may take slightly longer.

## ![Image 19: Bermuda company formation fees](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)Singapore Company Formation Fees

Your company will be incorporated using your chosen name and we will ensure that the procedure is as simple as possible.

**Singapore Pte Company Incorporation- 3 days**
*   Reserving your Company Name
*   Liaising with the local registrar and relevant authorities
*   Structuring the company as per your requirements
*   Prepare your Company Registration Forms
*   Drafting the Articles of Association / Statutes
*   File the documents with the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA)
*   Resident Director Security Deposit (£1750)
*   Initial Government licence fee payable on incorporation
*   Certificate of Incorporation
*   Issue of shares and production of Share Certificates
*   All documents and certificates supplied in a professional folder
*   Delivery of documents by FedEx / DHL courier£1640
Additional Services
Company Administration & Registered Office (required)£450
Provision of Nominee Local Director (required)£6500
Assistance with opening a Bank Account in Singapore£320
Provision of Corporate Secretary (required)£950
Resident Director Security Deposit£3500
Annual Renewal Fees
Provision of the Registered Office in Singapore£450
Company Secretarial Services£950
Renewal of Nominee Local Director£6500
Directors Register Maintenance£175

The whole incorporation process can be completed online, and we will administer the preparation and filing of all registration forms on your behalf.

## ![Image 21: company formation filing requirements](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)Filing Requirements

Companies are required to keep accounting records, but these may be kept anywhere in the world. Annual financial statements must be filed with the registry and tax authorities within seven months following the end of the accounting period. Generally, all companies must have their accounts audited with the audit report filed alongside the financial statement. All companies must file an annual return and pay the filing fee of SGD 20 (approximately EUR 12).

## ![Image 23: Bermuda company incorporation proof](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)Proof of Identity

As part of our due diligence, we require proof of identity in the form of a passport copy for all directors and shareholders of the company.

## ![Image 25: Bermuda Company formation travel](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)Travel

It is required to visit Singapore in order to incorporate a company.

# United Arab Emirates Company Formation

## ![Image 5: Bermuda Exempt Company](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/home-icon.png)United Arab Emirates Ras Al Khaimah (RAK) Company Formation

A Ras Al Khaimah (RAK) is equivalent to a Limited Liability Company in the UK or a GmbH in Austria and Germany in that it is a legal entity which is separate and distinct from the individuals who run it. For sole traders and for people in partnerships, the individuals’ personal assets are at risk if there is a claim against the organisation but shareholders in a RAK are liable to lose only the value of the share capital to which they subscribe.

An RAK can be set up in several ways; ‘LLC setup’ allows trade within the UAE and globally’, ‘Free zone setup’ offers visas and sponsorship, and ‘offshore setup’ offers tax free international trade and provides maximum confidentiality for the company’s beneficial owners.

The United Arab Emirates is one of the worlds’ fastest growing economies and has a very high standard of living, making the UAE an attractive location for incorporating companies and offering vast growth opportunities. Because of the various ways it can be setup, a Ras Al Khaimah is the most common form of incorporation in the UAE.

## ![Image 7: Bermuda company formation name](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/company_name.png)Company Name

Company names must be either derived from the primary business activities of the company or from one or more of the shareholders or directors names. The name must end with the suffix LLC or similar and the use of words depicting religious values or suggesting a connection with governmental bodies will be denied.

## ![Image 9: Bermuda company formation registered office](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Registered-Office.png)Registered Office

All companies registered in the UAE must have a registered office which must be a physical address in the UAE where official company documents may be legally served. We are able to provide a registered office as part of our incorporation package.

## ![Image 11: Bermuda Incorporation director](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Directors.png)Directors

To incorporate in the UAE a minimum of one director is allowed and a maximum of 50 directors is permitted. There are no residency or nationality restrictions and director registers are not available for public inspection.

## ![Image 13: Bermuda company formation shareholder](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Shareholders.png)Shareholders

Only one shareholder is required and may be of any nationality. Non-residents are not permitted to control more than 49% of a company registered in UAE so a majority shareholder must be resident in UAE. There is no maximum number of shareholders and corporate entities are permitted.

## ![Image 15: Bermuda company formation share capital](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Share-Capital.png)Share Capital

There is no minimum share capital requirement and the amount of chosen capital may be expressed in any currency.

## ![Image 17: company formation filing requirements](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)Filing Requirements

There is no obligation to file annual financial accounts or have accounts audited.

Incorporating is very quick; once we have received all the necessary documentation the process in complete in one to two working days.

## ![Image 3](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/home-icon.png)Bahamas International Business Company (IBC)

The Bahamas is a popular offshore jurisdiction because of its political-economic stability, privacy and tax benefits from which offshore companies benefit.

Bahamas Company Formations provides extensive confidentiality for the beneficial owners and shareholders enjoy exemption from a large number of taxes and duties including income tax, capital gains tax and corporation tax.

## ![Image 5](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/company_name.png)Company Name

Company names may be in any language that uses the Latin alphabet and must end with the suffix ltd, Corp, GmbH or similar. Panama is a popular offshore jurisdiction because of the large number of privacy and tax advantages from which offshore companies incorporated there benefit. Incorporating an IBC in Panama provides extensive confidentiality for the beneficial owners as company registers are not available for public inspection, and shareholders enjoy exemption from all local taxes and duties, including income tax, capital gains tax and corporation tax.

## ![Image 7: Bermuda company formation name](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/company_name.png)Company Name

A Panamanian IBC can have a name in any language provided that it is unique and that it ends with the following designations or their abbreviations: Corporation (Corp), Incorporated (Inc) or Sociedad Anónima (SA); the designation Limited (Ltd) may not be used. Formacompany can reserve your company name for up to 10 ten days.

## ![Image 9: Bermuda company formation registered office](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Registered-Office.png)Registered Agent

It is a requirement that a Panamanian IBC must have a registered agent and a registered address in Panama; this is where all official correspondence is sent. These are both provided as part of our incorporation service.

## ![Image 11: Bermuda Incorporation director](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Directors.png)Directors

A Panamanian IBC requires three directors. Director details are not filed on the public register.

## ![Image 13: Bermuda company formation shareholder](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Shareholders.png)Shareholders

A Panamanian IBC requires a minimum of one shareholder. Shareholders’ names are not filed on the public register.

## ![Image 15: Bermuda company formation share capital](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Share-Capital.png)Share Capital

The standard authorised share capital is US $10,000 divided into 100 common voting shares of USD 100 each or 500 common voting shares of no par value; the capital may be expressed in any convertible currency. The minimum issued capital is either one share of no par value or one share of par value. Share Capital does not have to be paid into a bank account before the incorporation.

## ![Image 17: company formation filing requirements](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Filing-Requirements.png)Filing Requirements

There is no need to file any company tax returns in Panama if all the income was derived from offshore transactions. There is no requirement to file financial statements if the income is from sources outside of Panama.

## ![Image 19: Bermuda company incorporation timescale](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)Timescale

The incorporation of a new company takes approximately one week from the date we receive proof of address and identification.

# Ready Made Companies

A ready made company will be beneficial if a company is required urgently, for instance, if a company registration number is needed immediately in order to complete an important contract and little time can be allowed for the incorporation process to be completed.

The companies have filed non-trading / dormant accounts together with their annual returns each year, have had no business activities and are in good standing.

They are available for immediate transfer and come with copies of all documents filed.

## Countries with Ready Made companies

*   [United Kingdom](https://www.formacompany.com/uk/uk-ready-made-company/)

## Shelf / Ready Made Company Benefits

*   Immediate availability – the company can be transferred to you on the same day, as the certificate of incorporation has already been previously delivered
*   Saving time – the only thing that needs to be changed when you buy a shelf company is the ownership, making the process simpler and faster than a new incorporation

## All of our Shelf / Ready Made companies:

*   Are Private Limited Companies
*   Can operate anywhere in the world
*   Offer shareholders limited liability
*   Can have a sole director and sole shareholder
*   Have an immediately available company registration number
*   Have wide objects and can be used for most business activities

## A Shelf/Ready Made Company includes:

*   Articles of Association /Statutes
*   Registered Office
*   Incorporation Certificate

## Procedure to acquire a Shelf / Ready Made Company

The company can be transferred to you and will be ready to trade immediately as soon as the new directors and shareholders sign the official forms in which they consent to act.

## Changing the company name of the Shelf / Ready Made Company

The Company Name can be changed, if required to your own choice of name.

We can also file a company name change if you require a certain business name of your very own choice – thus still affording you the old shelf company advantage and you can do any business that you wishs.

## Appointing the new Directors

You will need to sign a document confirming our resignation and appointing yourself as the new director, alternatively you can sign a Power of Attorney instructing us to sign the document on your behalf.

The company directors will be changed from our nominee staff directors to the directors of your choice and all the formation documents such as the Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association of the company and the relevant Company Secretarial Forms are also immediately available.

## Established /Shelf / Vintage Companies

Established Shelf Companies are companies that we incorporated ourselves in the previous years, but have never traded or carried out any business transactions. These companies can immediately be made available as the Incorporation Certificate has already been issued, and company bank accounts can also be immediately opened for the same reason.

We check the online companies registry service to confirm that your company name is acceptable and not already registered.

The registry will refuse a name if it is identical to, almost identical to or phonetically the same as an existing name or if it implies state sponsorship.

Use of certain words such as Bank, Insurance and Group will require special permission.

In the UK this service can be completed within 30 minutes of request but other jurisdictions may take far longer. In some cases this information is not available until a request to register a company is made.

### Meet the innovators

In 2015, Navan co-founders Ariel Cohen and Ilan Twig, tired of fighting with hard-to-use legacy travel and expense tools — and dealing with the resulting collateral damage — created a new corporate travel solution. The tool enabled users to easily book, view, and manage their travel and expenses in a single platform. Relentlessly innovative, the pair combined AI, data science, and a seamless user experience to take the first steps on the path toward building what would become Navan.

[Meet the leadership team](https://navan.com/about/leadership)

![Image 70: Ilan and Ariel Leadership Mobile](https://res.cloudinary.com/tripactions/image/upload/f_auto/c_limit/w_1230/q_auto/f_auto/q_auto/v1759870173/Ariel_Cohen_Ilan_Twig_2025_T_qekzaz.png)![Image 71: Ilan and Ariel Leadership Mobile](https://res.cloudinary.com/tripactions/image/upload/f_auto/c_limit/w_1230/q_auto/f_auto/q_auto/v1759870173/Ariel_Cohen_Ilan_Twig_2025_T_qekzaz.png)

We aim to revolutionize a decades-old industry and redefine how businesses and frequent travelers experience the world.

# Seychelles Company Formation

## ![Image 5: Bermuda Exempt Company](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/home-icon.png)The Seychelles International Business Company (IBC) Company Formation

The Republic of Seychelles is a popular offshore jurisdiction because of the large number of privacy and tax advantages from which offshore companies incorporated there benefit, following the Seychelles International Companies Act. Incorporating an IBC in the Seychelles provides extensive confidentiality for the beneficial owners as company registers are not available for public inspection, and shareholders enjoy exemption from all local taxes and duties, including income tax, capital gains tax and corporation tax.

## ![Image 7: Bermuda company formation name](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/company_name.png)Company Name

A company in the Seychelles must have a unique name, it may be in any language but the English translation must be approved. It must have a suffix of Corporation, Limited, Incorporated, GmBH, Societe Anonyme, or similar. The appropriate abbreviation can also be used.

## ![Image 9: Bermuda company formation registered office](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Registered-Office.png)Registered Agent

It is a requirement that a Seychelles IBC must have a registered agent and a registered address where all official correspondence may be sent. This is provided as part of our incorporation service.

## ![Image 11: Bermuda Incorporation director](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Directors.png)Directors

An IBC in the Seychelles requires only one director, this can be either an individual or a corporate entity and there is no restriction on nationality. As there is no public Director Register, directors’ details are confidential.

## ![Image 13: Bermuda company formation shareholder](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Shareholders.png)Shareholders

An IBC in the Seychelles requires only one shareholder there are no restrictions and nominee shareholders are permitted. As there is no public Shareholder Register, details of the company’s beneficial owners are confidential.

## ![Image 15: Bermuda company formation share capital](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Share-Capital.png)Share Capital

There is no minimum share capital and it may be expressed in any currency.

## ![Image 17: company formation filing requirements](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Filing-Requirements.png)Filing Requirements

All companies are required to keep a record of their accounts and a copy of these are to be provided to the Seychelles Agent. Accounts records are filed twice a year 31 July and 31 January.

Holding of accounting records fee will be included in the annual renewals.

A pre-formatted annual report is to be filed every year no later than 31 December.

## ![Image 19: Bermuda company incorporation timescale](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)Timescale

A Seychelles IBC can be incorporated in two days once all information and proof of identity have been accepted.

## ![Image 21: Bermuda company formation fees](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)Seychelles Company Formation Fees

## ![Image 23: Bermuda company incorporation proof](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)Proof of Identity

As part of our due diligence we require proof of identity in the form of a passport copy for all directors and shareholders of the company.

# Singapore Company Search & Documents[Document Order](https://www.formacompany.com/singapore-company-search/#document)

## **Singapore Company Search & Information Report**

**Seychelles Company Search:**

**Timescale:**Email copies sent within 3 – 5 working day

**Delivery:**PDF report sent via email only

A Singapore company search outlines the current administrative position of a Singapore company in accordance with the records held at the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA).

A company search report will include:

*   Company Name
*   Former Company Names – if applicable
*   Date of Change of Name – if applicable
*   Name effective date
*   Shareholders Details
*   Director Details
*   Date of Annual Return
*   Company Registration Number
*   Date of Incorporation/ Registration
*   Company Type – Limited Private company, Exempt Private company limited by shares
*   Company Status – live company, terminated, cancelled, gazetted to be struck off, dissolved
*   Status Date
*   Registered Address
*   Change of address date – if applicable
*   Principal Activity – company activities and description of the activities
*   Directors Reports and Accounts
*   Registry Compliance Rating – annual general meeting, annual return and accounts up-to-date, annual general meeting, annual return or accounts late, company status is not live
*   Principal place of Business
*   Constitution of Business
*   Date of change of address – if applicable

## Singapore Certificate of Good Standing (Electronic Only)

**Seychelles Certificate of Good Standing**

**Timescale:**Email copies sent within 5 – 9 working day

**Delivery:**PDF copies sent via email only

We can obtain an Electronic copy of a Singapore Certificate of Good Standing, the certificate is officially provided by the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority.

The Certificate certifies that the company is up to date with all administrative requirements under the Singapore Companies Act and has been in continues existence since incorporation.

The report bears the signature of an Assistant Registrar at the Singapore Registry

## Singapore Director’s Report & Accounts

**Singapore Director’s Report & Accounts Timescale:**Email copies sent within 2 – 5 working day | Courier depends on location

**Delivery:**PDF copies sent via email | Originals copies sent via courier

We can provide the latest Singapore Director’s Report & Accounts for any company registered in Singapore. The available Company accounts vary according to the classification of the company. The documents are obtained from the Singapore Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority.

The reports usually include:

*   directors’ report,
*   statement of financial position,
*   cash flow statement,
*   notes to the financial statements,
*   supplementary information,
*   profit and loss account,
*   balance sheets,
*   statement of comprehensive income
*   auditors’ report – if filed/ available as filing requirement depends on the type of company
*   a statement in changes in equity,

The format of the documents and reports is depending on the target company size and filing requirements.

## Order Company Documents

Please complete the order form with the target company name and registration number if known.

Documents are delivered by email as a PDF.

Please use the contact us link if you have any questions concerning Singapore documents, we will be pleased to assist you.

# Spain Company Formation

## ![Image 5: Bermuda Exempt Company](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/home-icon.png)Spanish Sociedad Limitada (SL) Company Formation

We have an office in Madrid very close to the Tax Office and Mercantile Registry and are able to liaise with the authorities to incorporate the company with the minimum of delay.

Incorporating an SL allows access to the lucrative Spanish market and Formacompany is uniquely qualified to help you establish and maintain your Spanish business. We have 20 years’ experience incorporating business in Spain and our Madrid office can facilitate everything from drafting the initial documentation for your company to processing and running the payroll for your employees.

## ![Image 7: Bermuda company formation name](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/company_name.png)Company Name

All company names must be approved by the Mercantile Register which takes around three days, once approved the name can be reserved for ten days free of charge. Company names must not be identical or deceptively similar to other companies already registered and the name must end with the suffix Sociedad Limitada or the abbreviation SL. It is recommended that at least three alternatives are supplied for checking.

## ![Image 9: Bermuda company formation registered office](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Registered-Office.png)Registered Office

All companies are required to have a registered office where official correspondence is sent We initially provide you with a registered office in Madrid, but this is easily changed to a location of your choice if required.

## ![Image 11: Bermuda Incorporation director](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Directors.png)Directors

Only one director is required for your company there is no restriction on either residency or nationality

All directors or shareholders will need Spanish identification numbers to sign the company statutes with the Notary; to be appointed as a director or shareholder you will require an identification number (NIE number), and for a corporate shareholder it is a CIF number.

*   We can obtain your fiscal identity number (NIE) for you
*   We can obtain a company tax number (CIF) for corporate shareholder

## ![Image 13: Bermuda company formation shareholder](https://www.formacompany.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Shareholders.png)Shareholders

Only a single shareholder is necessary, there are no restrictions on the nationality or residency of the shareholder and corporate shareholders are permitted.

An initial shareholder register is filed upon incorporation but any subsequent changes to shareholdings does not need to be filed.

## ![Image 15: Bermuda company formation share capital](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)Share Capital

A Spanish bank account is required to deposit the €3,000 share capital.

## ![Image 17: company formation filing requirements](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)Filing Requirements

Companies are required to file annual financial statements and an annual return. If the company is considered ‘small’ both these may be simplified and there is no requirement to appoint a statutory auditor.

## ![Image 19: Bermuda company incorporation timescale](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)Timescale

Once we have your proof of identity it takes only two weeks to incorporate your Sociedad Limitada in Spain.

## ![Image 21: Bermuda company formation fees](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)Spain Company Incorporation fees

**Spain SL Company Formation – 2 weeks**
Model 1: You need to visit Spain to sign documents in front of the notary

*   Liaising with the local registrar and relevant authorities
*   Structuring the company as per your requirements
*   Preparing your Company Registration Forms
*   Drafting Company Statutes to sign with a Notary
*   Filing the documents with the Registro Mercantil
*   Notarial Fees €400

*   All documentation provided will need to be translated into Spanish
*   Setting up the official minute book: with leather binder
*   All documents and certificates supplied in a professional folder
*   Delivery of documents by FedEx / DHL courier£1900
**Spain SL Company Formation – 2 weeks** Model 2: Where you wish to incorporate without visiting Spain
*   A Power of Attorney is organised with the notary so the company statutes can be signed by Formacompany

Company Administration

    *   Annual accounts in digital format

    *   Notes to the accounts

*   Annual legalisation of books of accounts

*   Mercantile Register: notifications of acceptance of documents, letters from Chamber of Commerce and letters from the authorities of the Municipality of place of business.

Directors Register Maintenance£175

Your company will be incorporated using your chosen name and we will ensure that the procedure is as simple as possible.

We will administer the preparation and filing of all registration forms on your behalf.

## ![Image 23: Bermuda company incorporation proof](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)Proof of Identity

As part of our due diligence we require proof of identity in the form of a passport copy for all directors and shareholders of the company.

## ![Image 25: Bermuda Company formation travel](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)Travel

Traveling to Spain is recommended as incorporation documents are usually signed before a notary in Spain and a bank account needs to be opened. If required we can draft a dual language Power of Attorney enabling us to sign documents on your behalf.

# How 21 big tech companies got their names

  

October 24, 2014 - 6:11 pm

## Tech company names

The expression ‘what’s in a name’ – or the slightly more poetic ‘a rose by any other name’ – means, essentially, that a name doesn’t matter. It suggests that it’s the attributes of a person or object that will dictate what it truly is and how it is seen by the world.

However, in the world of brands and big business, this isn’t necessarily the case. Company names need to encapsulate something personal but trustworthy. Or have to, at least, offer some relative merit over other options. Why is Nike (originally known as Blue Ribbon Sports) called Nike? Because it’s named after a mythological Greek goddess who personified victory. That sounds a lot better than Blue Ribbon Sports, doesn’t it?

With this in mind, we had a look at some of the biggest tech brands and the meaning behind how they got their names.

### Samsung

This is a pretty straight-forward one. The word Samsung in Korean means “[three stars](http://www.samsung.com/us/aboutsamsung/corporateprofile/history06.html)” and was chosen to represent the virtues of being“big, numerous and powerful” (like stars in the night sky, or so the story goes).

Samsung’s first products included dried fish, vegetables, noodles and fruit, although it obviously went on to diversify into a wide range of different industries. Today, it’s best known for smartphones and other consumer electronics, but over the years Samsung has entered the aerospace, insurance and financial industries, among others. It was only in 1987, with the passing of Samung’s founder[Lee Byung-chull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Byung-chull "Lee Byung-chull"), that the new CEO (Byung-chull’s son, Kun-Hee Lee) set sights on becoming a top 5 electronics manufacturer.

[![Image 15: Samsung Logo History Tech Company Names](https://media.thenextweb.com/2014/10/SamsungLogoHistory.avif)](https://thenextweb.com/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2014/10/SamsungLogoHistory.jpg)
Between 1938 and 1993, each Samsung logo actually featured the three stars in different forms. Since 1993, Samsung has been using its current logo, sans-stars.

* * *

### Nokia

Despite Nokia’s most recent fate in [bowing out of the smartphone market](https://thenextweb.com/news/microsoft-completes-acquisition-nokias-devices-services-business-price-slightly-higher-7-2b), it’s pretty widely known that it didn’t start life in the electronics business.

In fact, in 1865, its first operation was a wood pulp mill at the Tammerkoski Rapids in Finland. In 1868, seeking better water flow,the business opened another mill a few miles away from the town of Nokia on the banks of the Nokianvirta river, which is what inspired the name Nokia in 1871. Clearly, there was no rush for branding back in the late 19th Century.

[![Image 16: Nokia map tech company names](https://media.thenextweb.com/2014/10/Nokia_map.avif)](https://thenextweb.com/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2014/10/Nokia_map.png)

In 1967, it took the formal name of Nokia Coporation and was comprised of five different businesses: rubber, cable, forestry, electronics and power generation. Today, following its sale to Microsoft, there are three businesses left:Nokia Networks, HERE, and Nokia Technologies.

* * *

### Apple

As one of the world’s largest companies, Apple obviously attracts a fair amount of attention nowadays, but it wasn’t always that way.

In the video below, a much younger Steve Jobs explains how, when starting out, the company had to file “a fictitious business name statement” for official purposes. Suggestions included things like Matrix Electronics, but Apple Computer was finally settled on, with the proviso that it would become the company name if no one else had any better suggestions before the filing deadline.

So, why Apple? In Jobs’ own words: “Partially because I like Apples a lot and partially because Apple is ahead of Atari in the phonebook and I used to work at Atari”. In 2007,it dropped ‘Computer’ from the name to become just Apple.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qzzOwRx3D1E

Clearly, that plan worked pretty well – Apple is now a global powerhouse, while Atari bowed out of the hardware game long ago. As a bonus nugget, the name Atari comes from a Japanese verb meaning to hit the target, which is pretty apt for a gaming company.

* * *

### LG

Like many of the other companies here, LG Electronics didn’t start life with the name it now has. Instead, in 1958,GoldStar was founded in the aftermath of the Korean War with a remit to build electronic devices.

[![Image 17: Goldstar Logo tech company names](https://media.thenextweb.com/2014/10/Goldstar_logo21.avif)](https://thenextweb.com/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2014/10/Goldstar_logo21.png)

Sister-company to GoldStar was Lak-Hui (pronounced “Lucky”), and hence ‘Lucky Goldstar’ was born.This obviously contracts to the LG name we know today, and which is used for the tagline ‘Life’s Good’. In 1995, GoldStar officially adopted the LG brand and logo.

Now, the company says it just stands for LG, rather than either Life’s Good or Lucky Goldstar.

* * *

### HTC

Most people will tell you that HTC stands for High-Tech Computer, which it once did, but there’s another reason behind the name.

In 1997 when the company was founded by H.T. Cho (now chairman) and Cher Wang (now chairwoman) the two decided to use their own initials to form a name – and hence HTC was born.

[![Image 18: Cher Wang, co-founder (and the 'C') of HTC](https://media.thenextweb.com/2014/10/cherwang.avif)](https://thenextweb.com/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2014/10/cherwang.png)
Although admittedly the company _could_ have been named after H.T Cho alone and come up with the same result, anecdotally, an exec did once refer to Wang as ‘the C in HTC’ while in conversation with us.

**Next page:** Spotify, Sony and more

### Spotify

Spotify is an interesting one. Originally started in Sweden, the word Spotify doesn’t actually seem to mean anything in Swedish (although Google Translate does still attribute it to being Swedish).

Instead, the company’s founders Daniel Ek and Martin Lorentzon were sitting around one day trying to think of a name when one of the suggestions was misheard as ‘Spotify’, which then sort of just stuck. When the duo realized there were no Google results for the word and that the domains were available to register, they snapped them up and the rest is history.

[![Image 19: Spotify tech company names](https://media.thenextweb.com/2014/10/1024px-Spotify_HQ.avif)](https://thenextweb.com/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2014/10/1024px-Spotify_HQ.jpg)
As the company grew and gained popularity, an “afterconstruction” was sought to give a better story to how Spotify got its name. “We were a bit embarrassed to admit that’s how the name came up so our afterconstruction was to say that Spotify stems from SPOT and IDENTIFY,” [Ek wrote](https://www.quora.com/How-did-Spotify-get-its-name).

* * *

### Sony

The roots of Sony are another interesting blend of Latin and, well, English slang actually. More specifically, it’s a conjoining of ‘Sonus’, meaning sound and ‘Sonny’, meaning a well-to-do young man.

However, this wasn’t the original name. It was founded in 1946 under the name of Tokyo Tsushin Kogyo K.K (Tokyo Telecommunications Engineering Corporation),or simply Totsuko. Its mission was simply research at this point though.

[![Image 20: Sony type G](https://media.thenextweb.com/2014/10/Sony_type_G.avif)](https://thenextweb.com/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2014/10/Sony_type_G.jpg)
In 1947 it launched its first product, the “power megaphone” and in 1950 it released its first tape recorder – the ‘Type G’. Presumably, there were at least six failed attempts before that. (This is facetious, the G actually is a nickname for ‘government’ – a result of the recorder being used in courts and other official capacities.)

The name change came in the 1950s, when the company wanted to take its ambitions global, the trademark TTK belonged to another company. By combining Sonus and Sonny to come up with Sony, the company had an appropriate name without an existing trademark.

While the decision was taken to use the Sony logo on products in 1955, it wasn’t until 1958 that it became Sony Corporation.

* * *

### Nintendo

Nintendo is slightly trickier than many others here, so brace yourselves – you may never know the _true_ meaning.

Nonetheless, it’s widely cited and accepted that Nintendo comes from the literal translation of the Japanese meaning for “leave luck to fate”.

However, [_The History of Nintendo (1889-1980) – From Playing Cards to Game & Watch_](http://www.goodreads.com/book/show/12393199-the-history-of-nintendo-1889-1980---from-playing-cards-to-game-watch)by Florent Gorges, suggests that this interpretation might be incorrect. Instead, it suggests that it might be related to the company’s roots as a [‘Hanafuda’ playing card](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanafuda) manufacturer in the late 19th Century – [1889, to be precise](https://www.nintendo.co.uk/Corporate/Nintendo-History/Nintendo-History-625945.html). Hanafuda literally translates as “flower cards”.

What has that got to do with Nintendo?

According to the book, the company was looking to introduce a new line of cheaper cards and settled on the name ‘Tengu’. With Tengu being a mythological Japanese folklore often depicted with a large nose. Bear with it.

The word for “nose” (_hana_) is the same as the word for “flower” (_hana_) when transliterated into English.

[![Image 21: Nintendo cards tech company names](https://media.thenextweb.com/2014/10/Nintendo_cards.avif)](https://thenextweb.com/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2014/10/Nintendo_cards.jpg)
The History of Nintendo therefore says that Nintendo could then mean “the temple of free hanafuda”, as visitors to Osaka and Kyoto would rub their noses to signal a desire for gambling.

In an interesting summation of the issue, [Kotaku said](https://kotaku.com/5649625/nintendo-might-not-mean-what-you-think) that even Hiroshi Yamauchi, the great-grandson of the company’s founder, doesn’t know the truth behind the name, but that‘to leave one’s fortune in the hands of fate’ was a “plausible explanation”.

In 1933, it was formally established as Yamauchi Nintendo & Co. and later became Nintendo Playing Card Co. in 1951 before ultimately settling on Nintendo Co., Ltd.in 1963 – the same year it began making games alongside playing cards.

* * *

### Amazon

Amazon was nearly called Cadabra, as in ‘abracadabra’… as in the conjurer’s exclamation. Bezos wanted his book retail site to be so quick and easy that it seemed like magic.

Indeed, in 1994, this is exactly the name Jeff Bezos incorporated the company under, but the site went online in 1995 with the name of Amazon, taken from the Amazon River for being the biggest river. Clearly, Bezos had big ambitions right from the start.

The reason for the name change stemmed from a very legitimate fear that people could mishear cadabra.com as cadaver.com, [according to](https://books.google.co.uk/books?id=Nz43wixr2IcC&lpg=PA47&pg=PA46#v=onepage&q&f=false)the book _Jeff Bezos: The Founder of Amazon.com_ by Ann Byers.

[![Image 22: Amazon tech company names](https://media.thenextweb.com/2014/10/Amazon_HQ.avif)](https://thenextweb.com/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2014/10/Amazon_HQ.jpg)
Interestingly, [_The Everything Store: Jeff Bezos and the Age of Amazon_](https://www.amazon.co.uk/The-Everything-Store-Bezos-Amazon/dp/0552167835)by [Businessweek’s Brad Stone](http://www.businessweek.com/authors/411-brad-stone)suggests that Relentless.com was also another tabled suggestion, but that it seemed a little suspect.

“Bezos and his wife grew fond of another possibility: Relentless.com. Friends suggested that it sounded a bit sinister. But something about it must have captivated Bezos: he registered the URL in September of 1994, and he kept it,_”_[the book says](https://books.google.co.uk/books?id=3HIgAgAAQBAJ&pg=PA31&lpg=PA31&dq=Bezos+and+his+wife+grew+fond+of+another+possibility:+Relentless.com.+Friends+suggested+that+it+sounded+a+bit+sinister.+But+something+about+it+must+have+captivated+Bezos:+he+registered+the+URL+in+September+of+1994,+and+he+kept+it&source=bl&ots=kA-xOjOjBO&sig=mutAg8tW-XIZLUS9eZgxfmeXGMM&hl=en&sa=X&ei=cNdHVID4GMHQ7Ab93YDwCQ&ved=0CDQQ6AEwAw#v=onepage&q=Bezos%20and%20his%20wife%20grew%20fond%20of%20another%20possibility%3A%20Relentless.com.%20Friends%20suggested%20that%20it%20sounded%20a%20bit%20sinister.%20But%20something%20about%20it%20must%20have%20captivated%20Bezos%3A%20he%20registered%20the%20URL%20in%20September%20of%201994%2C%20and%20he%20kept%20it&f=false).

A quick whois lookup reveals the site is still associated with Amazon today and it still redirects to Amazon’s home page.

* * *

### Google

This one seems to be quite widely known: [Google took its name](https://web.archive.org/web/19990221202430/www.google.com/company.html) from a deliberate misspelling of Googol, the word that represents 10^100, or a 1 followed by 100 zeroes. Why this? Simply because founders Sergey Brin and Larry Page wanted to convey the huge amount of data they intended to make available.

The company registered the Google domain in September 1997 and incorporated the company a year later in September 1998.

[![Image 23: Google Beta tech company names](https://media.thenextweb.com/2014/10/GoogleBeta.avif)](https://thenextweb.com/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2014/10/GoogleBeta.png)

Less widely known is that [the nickname for the search engine was initially ‘BackRub’](http://web.archive.org/web/19961224105215/http://huron.stanford.edu/). Can you imagine if that had made it into every day parlance instead of Google? ‘Let me just BackRub that for you’, ‘I BackRubbed it.’

No.Nor can I.

In 2004, the estate of Edward Kasner, the mathematician that popularized the word Googol in the 1940 book[_Mathematics and the I_](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Mathematics-Imagination-Dover-Books/dp/0486417034)_[magination](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Mathematics-Imagination-Dover-Books/dp/0486417034),_ considered suing Google over its name. No suit was filed.

**Next page:**Microsoft, Facebook and more…

### Microsoft

Microsoft may be an engrained company brand nowadays, but back in 1975, the company was just a gleam in Bill Gates and Paul Allen’s eyes.

The company was officially established in April 1975, with the name coming from a combination of “microprocessor” and “software” – which is fitting given that they were creating software for the Micro Instrumentation and Telemetry Systems’s (MITS) Altair 8800.

[![Image 24: Altair8800 tech company names](https://media.thenextweb.com/2014/10/Altair8800.avif)](https://thenextweb.com/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2014/10/Altair8800.jpg)
In 1977, the company opened its first international office in Japan under the name of ASCII Microsoft. The company later incorporated in Washington to become Microsoft Inc.

Fun fact: Allen and Gates founded a business together before Microsoft called [Traf-O-Data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traf-O-Data)which looked at raw traffic data to create reports for engineers. While it wasn’t a runaway success, it was instructive of their later venture, which seems to have turned out a little better.

* * *

### Facebook

It’s hard to imagine many people _not_ knowing how Facebook got its name, given the level of scrutiny the company receives – and of course, [there was that movie](https://thenextweb.com/news/sean-parker-the-social-network-is-a-complete-work-of-fiction). Nonetheless, given the social colossus it has become, it’d be remiss to leave it out.

[![Image 25: Eisenberg, or 'not Zuckerberg', promoting The Social Network](https://media.thenextweb.com/2014/10/Eisenberg.avif)](https://thenextweb.com/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2014/10/Eisenberg.jpg)
In a nutshell, it’s simply the name of the directory of students some colleges in the US give to new starters so they can get to know a little about the people around them. And yes, it was thefacebook.com for about a year after launch in 2004, until the company registered Facebook.com in 2005.

* * *

### Mozilla

In 1994, when a team at Netscape sat around to think of names for a new browser to take on [NCSA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Center_for_Supercomputing_Applications)‘s Mosaic browser, what they were looking for was something that would crush the competition. What they looked to was Godzilla.

[![Image 26: MozillaORG](https://media.thenextweb.com/2014/10/MozillaORG.avif)](https://thenextweb.com/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2014/10/MozillaORG.png)
Combining Mosaic with the movie monster brings you to the current day name of Mozilla. Dave Titus designed the original Mozilla mascot above in 1994.

* * *

### Wikipedia

Wikiepedia’s settling on its name is a little more convoluted than some, as it started life – essentially – as Nupedia, a free online encyclopedia that was a byproduct of Jimmy Wales’ ad company [Bomis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bomis).

However, due to a heroically slow production of content (12 articles in the first year), the team looked to inspiration on how to speed up the process. The team settled upon the idea of using Ward Cunningham’s [WikiWikiWeb](http://c2.com/cgi/wiki/?WikiWikiWeb)(one of the first user-editable websites) to drum up interest in Nupedia by allowing people to edit and contribute content themselves.

[![Image 27: The WikiWikiWeb is still alive today.](https://media.thenextweb.com/2014/10/WikiWikiWeb.avif)](https://thenextweb.com/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2014/10/WikiWikiWeb.png)
Wales set on up on Jan 10, 2001. But that doesn’t fully explain the name. The word Wiki came into Web parlance as a result of Cunningham’s WikiWikiWeb, but he arrived at that name after landing in Honolulu Airport and being told to take the Wiki Wiki Shuttle. Wiki is[a Hawaiian word](http://www.mauimapp.com/moolelo/hwnwdshw.htm) for quick or fast.

* * *

### Asus

This is another simple one. Asustek, more commonly known as Asus, was founded by four former Acer employees in 1989 who derived the name from the mythological Greek winged horse Pegasus.

Why? That’s a fair question.

[![Image 28: Pegasus: the inspiration behind Asus' range of solid consumer electronics. Credit; Shutterstock](https://media.thenextweb.com/2014/10/Pegasus.avif)](https://thenextweb.com/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2014/10/Pegasus.jpg)
According to the company’s own explanation it “embodies the strength, purity, and adventurous spirit of this fantastic creature, and soars to new heights with each new product it creates.”

Hmm.

**Next page:**Lenovo, Hulu and more…

### Lenovo

When Lenovo’s founders sat around in 1984 to come up with a name, they left the meeting in agreement that it should be called“Chinese Academy of Sciences Computer Technology Research Institute New Technology Development Company,”[according to](https://books.google.co.uk/books?id=Mg7TdU9E3d0C&pg=PA26&lpg=PA26&dq=%22Chinese+Academy+of+Sciences+Computer+Technology+Research+Institute+New+Technology+Development+Company%22&source=bl&ots=so7cFhNF6_&sig=DKYDVtwjrAGz-xaxoJG83baHXQI&hl=en&sa=X&ei=jO9HVOPUHMOp7Abyv4CgCg&ved=0CCcQ6AEwAQ#v=onepage&q=%22Chinese%20Academy%20of%20Sciences%20Computer%20Technology%20Research%20Institute%20New%20Technology%20Development%20Company%22&f=false)_The Lenovo Affair_ by Zhijun Ling.

[![Image 29: LenovoLegend tech company names](https://media.thenextweb.com/2014/10/LenovoLegend.avif)](https://thenextweb.com/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2014/10/LenovoLegend.png)
Ultimately, [the group settled on Legend](http://www.legendholdings.com.cn/en/About/FullHistory.aspx) (in English), which is what the company was called for nearly two decades, until in 2003, it spun-out its own brand computer line into a separate business called Lenovo.

The word itself is a portmanteau of Le and Novo, meaning new in Latin.

* * *

### Hulu

While Hulu has no definition in English – or didn’t, at least – it has dual meanings in Mandarin, both of which appealed to former CEO Jason Kilar.

The first meaning is apprently used in an ancient Chinese proverb that “describes the Hulu as the holder of precious things” and literally translates to[gourd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gourd)– a plant that could be dried, hollowed out, and joined with another to create a container.

[![Image 30: Hulu tech company names](https://media.thenextweb.com/2014/10/shutterstock_158512259.avif)](https://thenextweb.com/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2014/10/shutterstock_158512259.jpg)
Kilar said the secondary meaning is ‘interactive recording’ and that “we saw both definitions as appropriate bookends and highly relevant to the mission of Hulu”.

As a bonus nugget, it also means upstream in Malay.

* * *

### Skype

Founded in 2003, Skype is another company that draws its name from the lack of availability of the name it _really_ wanted to use.

[![Image 31: Skype headquarters in Tallinn, Estonia. Credit: Shutterstock](https://media.thenextweb.com/2014/10/shutterstock_164876141.avif)](https://thenextweb.com/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2014/10/shutterstock_164876141.jpg)
You see, Skype is a rather straightforward combination of sky and peer-to-peer, shortened initially to Skyper, and then when that was already in use, to Skype. At least,[according to](http://web.archive.org/web/20070217033745/http://forum.skype.com/lofiversion/index.php/t5179.html) former Skype employee[Andreas Sjölund](https://twitter.com/asjolund).

* * *

### Twitter

This is another pretty well-known one. Twitter originally started out as twttr, inspired by Flickr, although early alpha user [@crystal](https://twitter.com/crystal), apparently suggested “FriendStalker” too, [according to](http://www.140characters.com/2009/01/30/how-twitter-was-born/) Dom Sagolla, a colleague at Odeo where Jack Dorsey and Ev Williams were also working.

But why twttr in the first place?

[![Image 32: An original sketch for the layout of twttr. Credit: Jack Dorsey/Flickr](https://media.thenextweb.com/2014/10/182613360_6d76db726a_o.avif)](https://thenextweb.com/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2014/10/182613360_6d76db726a_o.jpg)
“We did a bunch of name-storming, and we came up with the word ‘twitch,’ because the phone kind of vibrates when it moves. But ‘twitch’ is not a good product name because it doesn’t bring up the right imagery. So we looked in the dictionary for words around it, and we came across the word ‘twitter,’ and it was just perfect. The definition was ‘a short burst of inconsequential information,’ and ‘chirps from birds.’ And that’s exactly what the product was,” Dorsey told [the LA Times](http://latimesblogs.latimes.com/technology/2009/02/twitter-creator.html) in 2009.

* * *

### Yahoo!

[Founded in 1994](https://web.archive.org/web/20080713214826/http://yhoo.client.shareholder.com/press/timeline.cfm) as “Jerry and David’s Guide to the World Wide Web” by Jerry Yang and David Filo, Yahoo eventually took its name in January 1995, when the domain was purchased and the company was incorporated.

[![Image 33: Yahoo's website in 1996 via WayBackMachine](https://media.thenextweb.com/2014/10/Yahoo_1996.avif)](https://thenextweb.com/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2014/10/Yahoo_1996.png)
But rather than being based on the actual meaning of the word ‘yahoo’ ([a rude, noisy or violent person](http://www.oxforddictionaries.com/definition/english/yahoo)), Yahoo! is an acronym [Yet Another Hierarchical Officious Oracle](https://archive.today/puqz), although the founders did apparently like the general definition of yahoo, too. One of the categories in the screenshot above is [Yahooligans!](http://web.archive.org/web/19991112084013/http://www2.yahooligans.com/) (a Web guide for kids), too.

* * *

### SEGA

OK, so, admittedly SEGA isn’t the tech brand it once was, but it is still one a lot of people have nostalgic affection for.

[![Image 34: The SEGA SG1000 Credit Evan Amos / Wikimedia](https://media.thenextweb.com/2014/10/SEGA-SG1000.avif)](https://thenextweb.com/wp-content/blogs.dir/1/files/2014/10/SEGA-SG1000.jpg)
Although it was known as a Japanese gaming software and hardware giant,Sega’s roots began in Hawaii in 1940 as Service Games. [In 1951 the company moved to Tokyo](http://www.fundinguniverse.com/company-histories/sega-of-america-inc-history/), Japan to make coin-operated games and jukeboxes. Following a merger with rival Rosen Enterprises in 1965, the resulting company was known as SEGA Enterprises.

In 1986, Sega Enterprises went public in Japan and Sega of America, Inc. was established as a wholly owned subsidiary with the remit of adapting Sega’s Japanese video game products for American buyers. Still to this day, say SEGA, and many people just think ‘Sonic’.

Here is a guide for [naming your business](https://thenextweb.com/news/before-naming-your-startup-read-this) the right way.

**So there you have it, the back stories for some of the biggest names in tech. Did we miss your favorite? Let us know in the comments below or on our [Facebook page](https://www.facebook.com/thenextweb).**

### Meet the innovators

In 2015, Navan co-founders Ariel Cohen and Ilan Twig, tired of fighting with hard-to-use legacy travel and expense tools — and dealing with the resulting collateral damage — created a new corporate travel solution. The tool enabled users to easily book, view, and manage their travel and expenses in a single platform. Relentlessly innovative, the pair combined AI, data science, and a seamless user experience to take the first steps on the path toward building what would become Navan.

About Navan
Navan is the global AI-powered [business travel](https://navan.com/product/business-travel) and [expense management platform](https://navan.com/product/expense-management) that makes travel easy for frequent travelers. powering travel programs at more than 10,000 companies, including [Canva](https://navan.com/resources/case-study/canva-case-study-1), [HelloFresh](https://navan.com/resources/case-study/case-study-hellofresh), DoorDash, [Duolingo](https://navan.com/resources/case-study/duolingo-case-study), and Steelcase. The platform simplifies travel, payments, and expense management with intuitive tools for booking, automated payments with built-in virtual cards, and seamless expense reporting. Navan delivers [exceptional customer satisfaction](https://navan.com/reviews), with a 96% CSAT and 43 NPS. Founded in 2015 by Ariel Cohen and Ilan Twig as TripActions, Navan reported $613M in LTM revenue and $7.6B in LTM gross booking volume, each for the twelve months ended July 31, 2025. The company aims to empower organizations worldwide to make corporate travel smarter and more efficient. Learn more at [navan.com](https://navan.com/).

About Navan
Navan is the global AI-powered [business travel](https://navan.com/product/business-travel) and [expense management platform](https://navan.com/product/expense-management) that makes travel easy for frequent travelers. powering travel programs at more than 10,000 companies, including [Canva](https://navan.com/resources/case-study/canva-case-study-1), [HelloFresh](https://navan.com/resources/case-study/case-study-hellofresh), DoorDash, [Duolingo](https://navan.com/resources/case-study/duolingo-case-study), and Steelcase. The platform simplifies travel, payments, and expense management with intuitive tools for booking, automated payments with built-in virtual cards, and seamless expense reporting. Navan delivers [exceptional customer satisfaction](https://navan.com/reviews), with a 96% CSAT and 43 NPS. Founded in 2015 by Ariel Cohen and Ilan Twig as TripActions, Navan reported $613M in LTM revenue and $7.6B in LTM gross booking volume, each for the twelve months ended July 31, 2025. The company aims to empower organizations worldwide to make corporate travel smarter and more efficient. Learn more at [navan.com](https://navan.com/).

# Meet Olympians and Paralympians from the Sunshine Coast

AUS | 12 min read

1.   [Home](link_3)
2.   >[News](link_4)
3.   >Meet Olympians And Paralympians From The Sunshine Coast

There’s something in the salt air on the Sunshine Coast. Maybe it’s the 100km of golden coastline, the surf lifesaving culture, or the breezy sense of “you can do anything” that flows through every beach town and hinterland hill. Whatever it is, it seems to produce more than its fair share of sporting greatness.

From fearless first-timers to world record breakers, these 15 Sunshine Coast Olympians and Paralympians show what’s possible when resilience, passion and purpose come together.

## Alexa Leary

![Image 4: Image](link_5)

**Born:** 2001  
**Sport:** Para swimming  
**Games competed:** Paris 2024

After a life-changing cycling accident in 2021, Alexa didn’t just recover – she rewrote the script. The Noosa triathlete took up para swimming and stormed into Paris 2024 with gold in the 100m freestyle S9 and mixed 4×100m medley relay, plus silver in the mixed 4×100m freestyle. Alexa is now a world record holder and a true example of never giving up.

## Aly Bull

![Image 5: Image](link_6)

RIO DE JANEIRO, BRAZIL - AUGUST 15: Alyce Burnett (R) and Alyssa Bull (L) of Australia celebrate qualifying for the Final A after competing in the Canoe Sprint Women's Kayak Double 500m Semifinal 1 on Day 10 of the Rio 2016 Olympic Games at Lagoa Stadium on August 15, 2016 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. (Photo by Mark Kolbe/Getty Images)

**Born:** 1995  
**Sport:** Canoe sprint  
**Games competed:** Rio 2016, Tokyo 2020, Paris 2024

Growing up paddling the Sunshine Coast’s pristine waters, Aly was born for the surf. A former Ironwoman champ, she swapped the beach for the kayak and never looked back – making her Olympic debut at just 21.

Three Games later, she’s competed across K1, K2 and K4 500m events and added world titles to her name. When she’s not powering through water, she’s protecting lives as a Queensland firefighter. Now that’s Olympic spirit.

## Alyce Wood

![Image 6: Image](link_7)

**Born:** 1992  
**Sport:** Canoe sprint  
**Games competed:** Rio 2016, Tokyo 2020, Paris 2024

From Maroochydore SLSC nipper to world champion kayaker, Alyce has taken her surf roots all the way to three Olympic Games. With partner Aly Bull, she reached Olympic finals in Rio and Tokyo in the K2 500m, and capped her Olympic career with a solo run in the K1 500m B-final in Paris. Her legacy? Unstoppable.

## Brenden Hall

![Image 7: Image](link_8)

Brenden Hall AUS awaits the start of the Para Swimming Menâ€™s 400m Freestyle - S9 Final at the Paris La Defense Arena at the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games, Paris, France. Thursday 29 August 2024. Photo: OIS/Emma Da Silva. Handout image supplied by OIS/IOC

**Born:** 1993  
**Sport:** Para swimming  
**Games competed:** Beijing 2008, London 2012, Rio 2016, Paris 2024

Five Paralympics. Seven medals. Countless broken records. Brenden Hall OAM is Aussie swimming royalty. A powerhouse who competes across freestyle, backstroke and butterfly _plus_ relay teams.

After losing his leg at age six, Brenden turned challenge into champion form. In his Paralympic debut at 15 – as the youngest male competitor on the Aussie swim team – he broke the Paralympic Record in his heat in the 400m Freestyle S9. Adding several gold medals to his ever-growing tally in London and Rio, Brendan also scooped bronze at Paris 2024, proving champions never stop showing up.

## Callum Simpson

![Image 8: Image](link_9)

**Born:** 2007  
**Sport:** Para swimming  
**Games competed:** Paris 2024

At just 17, Callum burst onto the world stage with a double gold debut in Paris – dominating the 100m freestyle S8 and smashing the mixed 4×100m medley relay. Already an OAM recipient and crowned AIS Discovery of the Year 2024, this Alexandra Headland swimmer is a bright new force in Australian sport.

## **Clint Robinson**

**Born:** 1972  
**Sport:** Canoe sprint  
**Games competed:** Barcelona 1992, Atlanta 1996, Sydney 2000, Athens 2004, Beijing 2008

Five-time Olympian and Sunshine Coast surf legend, Clint made history as Australia’s first canoe sprint gold medallist, outpacing the world champ in a heart-stopping final in Barcelona 1992. Add a bronze and silver from later Games, 36 national surf titles, and a spot in the Sport Australia Hall of Fame – that’s the blueprint for a lifelong champion.

## Glynis Nunn

![Image 9: album slider image](link_10)

![Image 10: album slider image](link_11)

![Image 11: album slider image](link_12)

Los Angeles 1984 OG, Athletics, 100m hurdles Women - Qualification, Elissavet PANTAZIS (GRE), Sophia HUNTER (JAM), Edith OKER (FRG), Huajin LIU (CHN), Glynis NUNN (AUS) and Shirley STRONG (GBR) 2nd.

![Image 12: Previous](https://www.olympics.com/en/brisbane-2032/_next/static/media/button-arrow-left-black.551aa1ae.svg)![Image 13: Next](https://www.olympics.com/en/brisbane-2032/_next/static/media/button-arrow-right-black.e4de73f5.svg)

**Born:** 1960  
**Sport:** Athletics  
**Games competed:** Los Angeles 1984

Excelling in one Olympic discipline is tough. Try seven. Glynis Nunn made history winning gold in the heptathlon at LA 1984 – the only Aussie _ever_ to win a multi-event athletics title at the Olympics. From hurdles to javelin, she did it all with grace and grit. Her leap of faith (she quit teaching just a year out from the Games) paid off, big time.

## Jeff Hardy

![Image 14: Image](link_13)

© Sport the library/Bill Bachman Sydney 2000 Paralympic Games Swimming - Action shot of Jeff Hardy (AUS) in the pool (freestyle) as he takes a breath. Event unknown.

**Born:** 1959  
**Sport:** Para swimming  
**Games competed:** Atlanta 1996, Sydney 2000

A fierce competitor in the pool and three-time Paralympic gold medallist, Jeff Hardy OAM proved world-class swimming is all about heart and drive. At Atlanta 1996, he took home not one, but three medals – gold in the 400m freestyle B2 _and_ 100m butterfly B2, plus bronze in the 200m medley. He backed it up with another gold in the 400m freestyle S12 at Sydney 2000.

A world record holder in the 800m and 1500m freestyle, and a Sunshine Coast Sports Hall of Famer, Jeff’s legacy is as powerful as his stroke.

## Kaylee McKeown

![Image 15: Image](link_14)

NANTERRE, FRANCE - JULY 30: Kaylee McKeown of Team Australia celebrates after winning gold in the Women's 100m Backstroke Final on day four of the Olympic Games Paris 2024 at Paris La Defense Arena on July 30, 2024 in Nanterre, France. (Photo by Adam Pretty/Getty Images)

**Born:** 2001  
**Sport:** Swimming  
**Games competed:** Tokyo 2020, Paris 2024

Arguably Australia's greatest backstroker, Kaylee’s got talent in spades. At just 23, she’s collected nine Olympic medals – four of them gold – and became the second woman _ever_ to win both the 100m and 200m backstroke at consecutive Olympic Games. Honoured as Paris 2024 closing ceremony flag bearer, Kaylee isn’t just fast. She’s history-making.

## Korey Boddington

![Image 16: A cyclist stands next to his bike with a track in the background](link_15)

**Born:** 1995  
**Sport:** Para cycling  
**Games competed:** Paris 2024

Born in Mooloolaba, built for speed. Korey lit up Paris 2024 with a world record and gold medal in the C4 1000m time trial – plus bronze in the mixed team sprint C1-C5.

Fresh from setting another world record in the C4 Flying 200m at the 2025 Oceania Championships, keep your eyes on this rising rocket. There’s plenty more records in his sights.

Read more about Korey Boddington's story, and why he's known as the flying burrito, [here](link_16).

## Kyle Chalmers

![Image 17: Image](link_17)

Tokyo 2020 OG, Swimming, 100m freestyle Men - final. Kyle CHALMERS (AUS) 2nd.

**Born:** 1998  
**Sport:** Swimming  
**Games competed:** Rio 2016, Tokyo 2020, Paris 2024

Kyle Chalmers made a splash heard around the world at just 18, becoming the fourth Australian to win the coveted men’s 100m freestyle Olympic title – and our youngest Olympic swimming champion since Ian Thorpe.

From that breakout moment at Rio 2016, he’s cemented his place as one of Australia’s best sprint swimmers, picking up silver and bronze across three Olympic Games, including two medals at Paris 2024. Fierce, focused, and fast – Kyle’s a superstar who keeps delivering.

## Lisa Curry-Kenny

![Image 18: Image](link_18)

Los Angeles 1984 OG, Swimming, 200m individual medley Women - Qualification, Lisa CURRY (AUS).

**Born:** 1962  
**Sport:** Swimming  
**Games competed:** Moscow 1980, Los Angeles 1984, Barcelona 1992

Lisa dominated Aussie swimming in the ’80s and ’90s, the only Australian swimmer to hold Commonwealth and Australian records in every stroke except backstroke.

She proved herself a force of nature in the pool across three Olympics, scooping up seven Commonwealth Games golds along the way. After retirement? Lisa become a world champion in outrigger canoe racing, was awarded an OAM and inducted into Sport Australia Hall of Fame.

## Marayke Jonkers

![Image 19: Image](link_19)

BEIJING, CHINA - SEPTEMBER 14: (CHINA OUT) Marayke Jonkers of Australia celebrates in the award ceremony of Women's 150m IM - SM4 at the National Aquatics Center during day eight of the 2008 Paralympic Games on September 14, 2008 in Beijing, China. (Photo by China Photos/Getty Images)

**Born:** 1981  
**Sport:** Para swimming  
**Games competed:** Sydney 2000, Athens 2004, Beijing 2008

Making her Paralympic debut at Sydney 2000, Marayke broke over 70 national records, set a world record in the 100m butterfly, and brought home three Paralympic medals across three Games. But her biggest impact may be outside the pool. As a motivational speaker and passionate disability advocate, she’s showing Australia’s future athletes there’s more than one way to win.

## Melanie Wright (Schlanger)

![Image 20: Image](link_20)

Beijing 2008 OG, Swimming, 4x100m Freestyle relay Women - The Australian team (AUS) 3rd, from the left to the right: Melanie SCHLANGER, Alice MILLS, Cate CAMPBELL and Lisbeth TRICKETT.

**Born:** 1986  
**Sport:** Swimming  
**Games competed:** Beijing 2008, London 2012

One of the defining moments of London 2012? Melanie Wright anchoring Australia’s 4×100m freestyle relay team to an unforgettable gold. With Alicia Coutts, Cate Campbell, and Brittany Elmslie, the quartet stormed to victory in world-class style – holding off a fast-finishing Dutch team and smashing the Olympic record in the process. It was Australia’s only swimming gold of the Games and an electric moment for the nation.

Across her two Olympic appearances, Melanie collected five medals (two gold, two silver, one bronze) and an OAM – the kind of career that makes waves in every sense.

## Ryley Batt

![Image 21: Image](link_21)

Ryley Batt AUS moves away from Aaron Phipps GBR during the Wheelchair Rugby - Open - Bronze Medal Game at the Champ-de-Mars Arena at the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games, Paris, France. Monday 2 September 2024. Photo: OIS/Adrian Dennis. Handout image supplied by OIS/IOC

**Born:** 1989  
**Sport:** Wheelchair rugby  
**Games competed:** Athens 2004, Beijing 2008, London 2012, Rio 2016, Tokyo 2020, Paris 2024

It was a school visit from two-time Paralympian Brad Dubberley that first inspired Ryley Batt OAM to pursue wheelchair sports. Just three years later, aged 15, he represented Australia as the youngest ever wheelchair rugby player at the Paralympic Games.

Ryley’s story is the stuff of sporting folklore. Fast-forward two decades and he’s built a career as one of the fiercest – and most admired – players in global wheelchair rugby. The history-making athlete has competed at six Paralympic Games, including leading the Aussies to back-to-back gold medals at London 2012 and Rio 2016, became co-captain of the entire Australian Paralympic Team at Tokyo 2020, and even inspired a Netflix doco appearance in _Rising Phoenix_.

**The Sunshine Coast has a depth of athletic talent. Read on to discover more Olympians and Paralympians below:**

*   Emily Beecroft PLY - Para Swimming - Paris 2024, Tokyo 2020, Rio 2016
*   Ricky Betar PLY - Para Swimming - Paris 2024, Tokyo 2020

# Welcome to [Wikipedia](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:About "Wikipedia:About"),

the **free [encyclopedia](link_12)** that [anyone can change](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Introduction "Wikipedia:Introduction").

Search the [285,448](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Statistics "Special:Statistics") articles in the [Simple English Wikipedia](link_13)

[How to write Simple English pages](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:How_to_write_Simple_English_pages "Wikipedia:How to write Simple English pages")**·**[Useful pages](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Useful_pages "Wikipedia:Useful pages")**·**[Simple talk](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Simple_talk "Wikipedia:Simple talk")**·**[Categories](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:CategoryTree "Special:CategoryTree")**·**[Help](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Contents "Help:Contents")  
[Schools Gateway](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Schools "Wikipedia:Schools") (for users who want to make changes from a school)

## About Wikipedia

This is the front page of the **[Simple English Wikipedia](link_13)**. _Wikipedias_ are places where people work together to write [encyclopedias](link_12) in different languages. We use [Simple English](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Simple_English_Wikipedia#Simple_English "Wikipedia:Simple English Wikipedia") words and [grammar](link_14) here. The Simple English Wikipedia is for everyone, such as children and adults who are learning English. There are 285,448 articles on the Simple English Wikipedia. All of the pages are [free to use](link_15). They have all been published under both the _[Creative Commons Attribution/Share-Alike License 4.0 International License](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Text\_of\_the\_Creative\_Commons\_Attribution-ShareAlike\_4.0\_International\_License "Wikipedia:Text of the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License")_ and the _[GNU Free Documentation License](link_16)_. **You can help here!** You may change these pages and make new pages. Read the [help pages](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Contents "Help:Contents") and other [good pages](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Useful "Wikipedia:Useful") to learn how to [write pages here](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:How_to_write_Simple_English_articles "Wikipedia:How to write Simple English articles"). If you need help, you may ask questions at [Simple talk](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Simple_talk "Wikipedia:Simple talk").

* * *

When writing articles here:

*   **Use [Basic English](link_17) words and shorter sentences.** This allows people to understand complex terms or phrases.
*   **Write good pages.** The best encyclopedia pages have useful, well-written information.
*   **Use the pages to learn and teach.** These pages can help people learn English. You can also use them to [make a new Wikipedia](link_18) to help other people.
*   **Simple does not mean short.** Writing in Simple English means that simple words are used. It does not mean readers want basic information. Articles do not have to be short to be simple; expand articles, add details, but use basic [vocabulary](link_19).
*   **Be bold!** Your article does not have to be perfect because other editors will fix it and make it better. And most importantly, do not be afraid to start and make articles better yourself.
## Selected Very Good Article [![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=simple.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cscr-featured.svg)

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b9/Neptune_Voyager2_color_calibrated.png/250px-Neptune_Voyager2_color_calibrated.png?utm_source=simple.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Neptune_Voyager2_color_calibrated.png)

**[Neptune](link_20)** is the eighth and farthest [planet](link_21) from the [Sun](link_22) in the [Solar System](link_23). It is an [ice giant](link_24). It is the fourth-largest planet in the system.

Neptune's [mass](link_25) is 17 times [Earth's](link_26) mass and a little bit more than [Uranus'](link_27) mass. Neptune is denser and smaller than Uranus. Its greater mass makes its [gravity](link_28) make its [atmosphere](link_29) smaller and [denser](link_30).

It was named after the [Roman god](link_31) of the sea, [Neptune](link_32). Neptune's astronomical symbol is ♆, the [trident](link_33) of the god Neptune.

Neptune's atmosphere is mostly [hydrogen](link_34) and [helium](link_35). It also contains small amounts of [methane](link_36) which makes the planet appear blue. Neptune's [blue](link_37) color is much darker than the color of [Uranus](link_38). Neptune also has the strongest winds of any planet in the Solar System, as high as 2,100 km/h or 1,300 mph.

[Urbain Le Verrier](link_39) and [John Couch Adams](link_40) were the [astronomers](link_41) who discovered Neptune. Neptune was not discovered using a [telescope](link_42). It was the first planet to be discovered using [mathematics](link_43). In 1821, astronomers saw that [Uranus](link_27)' orbit was different from what they expected. Another nearby planet's mass was changing Uranus' orbit. They found Neptune was the cause.

_[Voyager 2](link_44)_ visited Neptune on 25 August 1989. It was the only [spacecraft](link_45) to visit the planet. Neptune used to have a huge storm known as the "[Great Dark Spot](link_46)". Voyager 2 discovered the spot in 1989. The dark spot was not seen in 1994, but new spots were found since then. It is not known why the dark spot disappeared. Visits by other [space probes](link_47) have been planned.

Neptune has five rings. These rings are hard to see from the Earth.

A satellite image of Hurricane Floyd in 1987

**[Hurricane Floyd](link_49)** was the only [hurricane](link_48) to make [landfall](link_50) in the United States during the [1987 Atlantic hurricane season](link_51). It was the last of seven [tropical storms](link_52) and three [hurricanes](link_48). Floyd developed on 9 October just off the east coast of [Nicaragua](link_53). Floyd was a hurricane for only twelve hours. It [dissipated](link_54) on 14 October.
